5. **Risk and Reward**: Buying a put option involves lower risk than short-selling the underlying stock because if the stock price falls below the strike price, you can exercise the option. The maximum loss you can incur is the premium paid, assuming the option expires worthless. On the other hand, buying a put option can give you significant leverage due to the fact that your upside is limited to the premium, whereas your downside is unlimited if the stock rises dramatically.

6. **Exercise**: You can choose to exercise (buy) or let the option expire if you do not hold the underlying stock and the stock price falls to or below the strike price before the expiration date.
